title: Valuatively bounded generic points and the integral subgroup
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $L$ a field [def-weil-field] with an $R$-algebra structure. Let $\mathcal D$ be a group scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Define its generic points as $R$-scheme morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\mathcal D$, with the group law induced by the group diagrams. By the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], these are the $L$-points of $G=\mathcal D\times_R\operatorname{Spec}L$. Define the integral-point subgroup to be the image of the group homomorphism $\mathcal D(R)\to G(L)$ obtained by precomposition with $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. For a generic point $x$, evaluation of $f\in\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)$ is pullback along the corresponding $\operatorname{Spec}L\to G$, followed by $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}L,\mathcal O)=L$. For an additive valuation $v:L\to\mathbf Z\cup\{+\infty\}$ with $v(0)=+\infty$, a subgroup $M\subseteq G(L)$ is valuatively bounded when for every $f\in\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)$ there exists $n_f\in\mathbf Z$ such that $n_f\leq v(f(x))$ for every $x\in M$.
